item.title: Stop1 Pride
item.description:
Stop1 Pride was the most ambitious party we threw as a collective. The party stretched 13 hours, had two stages, 12 artists, and onsite food. There were also countless roadblocks, such as melted DJ equipment from the previous party, a DJ with corrupted files, and general chaos.

However, it was our best party yet as a collective. We learned from Stop1 XL that having a dedicated door person alleviated so much stress for the team. Instead of trying to pack out the winery, we converted it into a chill-out room filled with beanbags, carpet, and food and were able to keep people within the club for several more hours than we otherwise would have.

item.title: Stop1 XL
item.description: Stop1 XL was our second party at Honey’s. The reason it was referred to as Stop1 XL was because we decided to use both the rooftop and winery within the venue. Given this extra space, we were able to book several new faces. The party was a success, with over 400 guests, but we learned that the roof of Honey’s is just extremely desirable, and it was challenging to fill out both rooms. We took this lesson with us to the following party.

item.title: Stop1 One Year
item.description:
Stop1 One Year was our last event at Hellphone. For the event, we brought back all of the artists who had contributed to the party over the past year. It was also our most ambitious lighting and design project.

Over the year, the party started off with a few dozen people, eventually overfilling the club. It was the first time we had a line all night and showed that keeping with an event and deeply caring about it inevitably leads to its growth.
